steps.intent: Panama's primary objective is to maintain Council consensus by securing the timely, 12-month renewal of the targeted sanctions regime (travel ban, asset freeze) and arms embargo, alongside a 13-month extension of the Panel of Experts' mandate, to cut off the weapons and financing pipelines fueling Haitian gangs. The main points expected to be sensitive during negotiations are balancing demands for enhanced regional border inspections and arms-tracing accountability (strongly favored by China and CARICOM members) against sovereignty and commercial sensitivities, as well as referencing the recently authorized Gang Suppression Force (resolution 2793) without alienating members who abstained on that deployment.

messages.Algeria: Algeria fully supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and arms embargo, which are crucial to curtailing the capacity of criminal gangs terrorizing the Haitian population. We believe the draft should explicitly address countries of origin regarding illicit arms flows to enhance the effectiveness of the embargo, while underscoring the imperative of addressing the socio-economic root causes of instability. We look forward to working constructively with the penholders towards a swift consensus adoption.
messages.China: China has consistently championed the strict implementation of the arms embargo and targeted sanctions as vital tools to stem the violence plaguing Haiti. To address the crisis effectively, the Council must tackle the root of the problem by demanding that countries of origin take concrete domestic action and tighten export controls to stop illicit weapons and ammunition from flooding into Haiti. Furthermore, language regarding recent Council decisions on mission transitions where consensus was lacking should be adjusted to maintain the broad unity of this Council on the sanctions regime.
messages.Denmark: Denmark expresses strong appreciation to Panama and the United States for circulating this draft renewing the Haiti sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which are vital tools to curb illicit arms flows and destabilizing gang activity. To further align the text with Council priorities, we encourage explicit reaffirmation of the humanitarian carve-out under resolution 2664 (2022) and tasking the Panel of Experts to report on grave violations against children and sexual and gender-based violence. Denmark looks forward to supporting this resolution.
messages.France: France thanks Panama and the United States for circulating this balanced draft and fully supports the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts. We propose two minor adjustments to ensure seamless legal clarity for the MSS mission alongside the GSF during the ongoing transition, and to reflect the important role of UNODC in tracking and stemming illicit arms flows. France stands ready to work with the co-penholders for a swift and unanimous adoption.
messages.Greece: Greece strongly supports the draft resolution and commends Panama and the United States for their leadership in renewing the sanctions regime and arms embargo. To maintain Council consistency and robust accountability, we propose reinforcing OP4 and OP6 with explicit references to serious human rights abuses, specifically sexual and gender-based violence and violations against children. We stand ready to support the swift adoption of this text.
messages.Guyana: Guyana strongly supports the renewal of the Haiti sanctions regime and the territorial arms embargo, which remain vital tools to curb the intolerable level of gang violence plaguing our sister Caribbean nation. To maximize effectiveness, we must address the entire supply chain of illicit firearms by calling on countries of origin and manufacture, as well as transit hubs, to bolster export controls and tracing. Furthermore, institutionalizing operational cooperation with CARICOM IMPACS and UNODC alongside INTERPOL will ensure robust regional information-sharing and enforcement.
messages.Pakistan: Pakistan fully supports the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo, which remain vital instruments to curb gang violence and restore stability in Haiti. To effectively dry up the resources of criminal gangs, it is essential that the resolution places adequate emphasis on stemming the illicit flow of weapons and ammunition at their source and transit points, while keeping child protection central to Council actions. We hope these constructive proposals can be integrated to ensure a strong, consensual outcome.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea expresses its strong appreciation to the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for timely circulating this balanced draft resolution. Renewing the sanctions regime, including the targeted measures and the arms embargo, alongside the mandate of the Panel of Experts, is vital to stemming the illicit flow of weapons that fuels gang violence in Haiti. We fully support the draft text as it stands and stand ready to vote in favor of its prompt adoption.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation supports the continuation of the targeted sanctions regime and the arms embargo to curb the rampant criminal violence in Haiti. However, the resolution must explicitly address the primary source of illicit firearms and ammunition flooding the country and demand accountability from countries of origin. We also recall that our delegation abstained on resolution 2793 (2025), and the text should reflect a balanced approach centered on a Haitian-led political resolution rather than overly endorsing external security formulas.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone welcomes the draft resolution presented by Panama and the United States renewing the sanctions regime and arms embargo, which remain vital tools to curb gang violence and support the stabilization of Haiti. We emphasize the necessity of explicitly addressing source countries of illicit weapons and reinforcing cooperation with regional bodies like CARICOM IMPACS to halt weapons proliferation at its roots. Furthermore, we urge the Council to highlight accountability for grave violations against children and conflict-related sexual violence within the Committee's designation priorities.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the draft resolution and the timely renewal of the Haiti sanctions regime, the arms embargo, and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. To further align the text with the Council's established focus on the protection of civilians, we propose modest additions to explicitly ensure gender and child protection perspectives are systematically integrated into the Panel's reporting and designations framework. We look forward to working constructively with Panama and the United States toward the prompt adoption of this text.
messages.Somalia: Somalia commends Panama and the United States for preparing this balanced draft renewing the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Haiti. Drawing from our own national experience, we emphasize that strictly stemming the illicit flow and trafficking of weapons and ammunition to gangs is vital for restoring peace and rule of law. We fully support the draft text as presented and look forward to its unanimous adoption.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom strongly supports the draft resolution extending the Haiti sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, and we thank the United States and Panama for their continued leadership. Robust sanctions and an effective arms embargo remain indispensable tools to choke off the supply of weapons and illicit finance to armed gangs. We propose a minor addition to operative paragraph 4 to ensure explicit Council focus on designating those responsible for horrific acts of sexual and gender-based violence and abuses against children.
messages.United States of America: As co-sponsor of this draft resolution alongside Panama, the United States strongly supports the text as circulated. This draft provides essential continuity by renewing targeted sanctions and the arms embargo to starve armed gangs of weapons and illicit financing while fully safeguarding support to Haitian security forces and authorized missions like the MSS and the GSF. We urge all Council members to support this text and work toward a swift and unanimous adoption.

before.Panama:
(spoke in Spanish)

Panama, together with our co-penholder, the United States, is pleased to present to the Security Council the draft resolution before us today, which renews the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Haiti established pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022).

The situation in Haiti remains critical. Illicit flows of weapons, ammunition, and illicit financing continue to fuel the terror inflicted by criminal gangs on the Haitian people, resulting in grave human rights abuses, including horrific levels of sexual violence and the recruitment and abuse of children. Targeted sanctions and a robust, effectively enforced arms embargo are vital, indispensable tools to disrupt the supply lines of these gangs and hold accountable those who finance and arm violence. 

The draft resolution before us strengthens cooperation to stem illicit arms trafficking, calls on Member States to redouble border and customs controls, and directs the Sanctions Committee to continue updating designations against those undermining Haiti's peace, stability, and democratic restoration. It also ensures that the Panel of Experts can continue its invaluable investigative reporting.

In presenting this text, Panama reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with our sister Republic of Haiti and the Haitian people. We urge all members of the Security Council to vote in favour of this draft resolution.

after.China:
(spoke in Chinese)

China voted in favour of the resolution just adopted. 

The security and humanitarian situation in Haiti remains grave, with criminal gangs continuing to run rampant, wreaking havoc on the lives and livelihoods of the Haitian people. Illicit flows of weapons and ammunition from abroad are the primary fuel sustaining gang violence in Haiti. Cutting off the supply of weapons and financial lifelines to these gangs is of paramount importance to restoring peace and stability in Haiti.

China has consistently supported the Security Council in taking necessary and robust measures to address the situation in Haiti. The unanimous adoption of this resolution demonstrates the Council’s united determination to curb gang violence and support the Haitian people. 

Resolutions are not meant to remain merely on paper; the key lies in their comprehensive and effective implementation. China calls on all Member States, especially regional countries and countries of origin and transit, to effectively implement the arms embargo. They must take concrete and effective domestic measures to tighten border and port controls, stem the illicit trafficking of firearms and ammunition into Haiti at the source, and ensure that no weapons fall into the hands of criminal networks. 

At the same time, the 2653 Sanctions Committee should accelerate its work to update and expand the sanctions list, targeting gang leaders, their political and financial sponsors, and those who illicitly supply weapons. The Panel of Experts should continue to objectively and impartially carry out its mandate, track the sources and routes of illicit arms and financial flows, and provide actionable information to assist the Council and the Committee.

Ultimately, the solution to the crisis in Haiti lies in the hands of the Haitian people themselves. We urge all political parties and factions in Haiti to put the interests of the country and its people first, advance an inclusive Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue, and restore constitutional order at an early date. China stands ready to continue working with the international community to support Haiti in finding a lasting path toward stability, development, and peace.

Thank you, Madam President.
after.France:
(spoke in French):

France welcomes the unanimous renewal of the sanctions regime and the extension of the mandate of the Panel of Experts on Haiti. We thank Panama and the United States for their dedicated work as co-penholders in guiding the Council to this consensus.

The unanimous adoption of this resolution sends a clear and united message: the international community will not tolerate impunity for those who finance, arm, and fuel the terror inflicted by criminal gangs upon the Haitian people. 

The sanctions regime, and in particular the targeted arms embargo, is an essential instrument for restoring stability in Haiti. It is intolerable that gangs continue to obtain heavy weapons and ammunition with which they murder civilians, recruit children, carry out horrific acts of sexual violence, and undermine the state's institutions. We urge all Member States, particularly regional and transit countries, to strictly implement the arms embargo and redouble their efforts to stem the illicit trafficking of arms and ammunition at their source.

Furthermore, France fully supports the expansion of targeted listings to hold accountable both the gang leaders on the ground and their political and economic sponsors who orchestrate instability from behind the scenes. We commend the diligent work of the Panel of Experts, whose reporting remains crucial for the Sanctions Committee's designations.

This decision comes just weeks after the Council’s adoption of resolution 2793 (2025), which authorized the transition of the Multinational Security Support mission into the Gang Suppression Force. Sanctions and security support must go hand in hand. Alongside our support for the Haitian National Police and the security forces on the ground, France will continue to stand firmly with the Haitian people in their pursuit of lasting peace, justice, and the restoration of democratic institutions through free and fair elections.
after.Guyana:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the members of the A3+, namely Algeria, Sierra Leone, Somalia, and my own country, Guyana.

We welcome the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the Haiti sanctions regime and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We extend our sincere appreciation to the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for their constructive and inclusive leadership throughout the negotiation process, which has once again enabled this Council to speak with one united voice.

The renewal of these targeted measures is a vital expression of the Security Council’s continued resolve to stand with the people of Haiti in the face of relentless gang violence, lawlessness, and severe humanitarian distress. The illicit trafficking of weapons, ammunition, and illicit financial flows remains the principal lifeline sustaining criminal networks that terrorize Haitian communities. By renewing and reinforcing the arms embargo and targeting those who finance, arm, and orchestrate this violence, the Council sends an unequivocal message that impunity will not be tolerated.

We particularly welcome the continued emphasis on stemming illicit weapons flows at their source and transit points, and we urge all Member States, especially regional partners and countries of origin, to fully implement their obligations under the arms embargo, including through rigorous border management, customs control, and tracing cooperation with regional mechanisms such as the CARICOM Implementation Agency for Crime and Security (IMPACS) and UNODC.

The A3+ remains deeply alarmed by the catastrophic humanitarian situation and the egregious violations of human rights perpetrated by armed gangs, including alarming levels of sexual and gender-based violence used as a tool of terror, and the systematic recruitment and exploitation of children, who represent an unconscionable portion of gang ranks. We welcome the explicit instruction to the Panel of Experts to continue integrating analysis on these violations and urging that child protection and the protection of vulnerable populations remain central to our collective response.

Sanctions are not an end in themselves; they must function in tandem with broader, comprehensive efforts to restore security, stability, and democratic governance. Following our recent adoption of resolution 2793 (2025) authorizing the transition to the Gang Suppression Force and establishing a dedicated UN support office, today’s renewal of sanctions provides crucial reinforcement to Haiti’s security architecture and the efforts of the Haitian National Police. 

In conclusion, the A3+ reaffirms that sustainable peace in Haiti can only be achieved through an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political process. We reaffirm our full solidarity with the Haitian people and our enduring commitment to supporting their journey toward constitutional order, security, and long-term prosperity.

I thank you.
after.Pakistan:
Mr. President,

Pakistan voted in favour of the resolution just adopted, renewing the sanctions regime on Haiti and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. 

Our affirmative vote reflects Pakistan’s steadfast commitment to supporting the people of Haiti in overcoming the severe security, political, and humanitarian crises gripping their country. 

The rampant gang violence, grave human rights abuses—particularly against women and children—and the breakdown of essential services continue to inflict immense suffering on the Haitian population. To curb this violence, it is critical to stem the illicit flow of small arms, light weapons, and ammunition that fuel the criminal networks destabilizing Haiti. We welcome the resolution’s emphasis on strengthening border, maritime, and aerial controls, and we urge all Member States, particularly regional states and countries of origin and transit, to effectively implement the arms embargo.

At the same time, sanctions and security-related measures are tools, not an end in themselves. A sustainable solution to Haiti’s multifaceted challenges requires addressing the underlying socioeconomic drivers of instability, including poverty, inequality, and institutional weakness. Above all, it requires an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue aimed at restoring constitutional order, strengthening democratic institutions, and paving the way for free, fair, and credible elections.

Pakistan remains committed to engaging constructively with all Council members and partners to support a peaceful, stable, and prosperous future for Haiti.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Panama:
(spoke in Spanish)

Panama welcomes the unanimous adoption of this resolution and wishes to express its sincere gratitude to all members of the Security Council for their constructive engagement, flexibility, and strong support throughout the negotiation process. We also extend our deep appreciation to our co-penholder, the United States, for its excellent cooperation and joint leadership.

Today’s unanimous vote sends an unequivocal message of unity and solidarity from the Security Council to the people of Haiti. At this critical juncture, as the transition toward the Gang Suppression Force authorized by resolution 2793 (2025) gets underway, targeted sanctions and a robust arms embargo are indispensable instruments in our collective effort to dismantle the networks of violence, cut off the illicit supply of arms and ammunition, and hold accountable those who finance and fuel instability. 

We urge all Member States, particularly countries of origin and transit, to rigorously enforce the measures reaffirmed today and to cooperate fully with the 2653 Sanctions Committee and the Panel of Experts. Panama remains steadfastly committed to supporting Haiti on its path toward security, institutional restoration, and sustainable peace.
after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian)

The Russian Federation voted in favour of the resolution renewing the targeted sanctions regime on Haiti, including the arms embargo, and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. 

We consistently support international efforts aimed at countering the rampant gang violence that continues to inflict untold suffering on the Haitian people. A properly calibrated sanctions regime, when applied objectively and effectively, remains an essential instrument in disrupting the illicit financial and operational networks that fuel criminal gangs.

At the same time, we must reiterate what has long been obvious: the primary catalyst of the catastrophic security crisis in Haiti is the uninterrupted flow of illicit firearms and ammunition. It is no secret where these weapons are coming from. The overwhelming majority of the firearms, including high-caliber military-grade weapons that allow gangs to overpower national law enforcement, are trafficked from the territory of the United States, particularly from ports in Florida. 

While the resolution once again calls upon Member States, especially countries of origin, to implement strict export controls and border measures, declarations on paper are clearly insufficient. What is urgently needed are tangible, resolute domestic actions by the United States authorities to halt the smuggling of weapons and ammunition from their territory into Haiti. Without effectively cutting off this illicit supply chain, all other international efforts, including security deployments under ever-changing titles, will remain futile.

Furthermore, we emphasize that the sanctions mechanism must be applied strictly in accordance with its mandate and based on verified, objective information. Sanctions must target not only low-level gang leaders, but also the influential political and economic figures who sponsor, arm, and manipulate these criminal groups for their own ends. 

In conclusion, we reaffirm that sustainable stabilization in Haiti cannot be achieved through punitive measures or external security assistance alone. Long-term peace requires addressing the deep-seated root causes of instability, strengthening national state institutions—primarily the Haitian National Police—and fostering an inclusive, Haitian-led political dialogue aimed at restoring constitutional order and holding long-overdue democratic elections.
after.Sierra Leone:
I have the honour to deliver this statement on behalf of the three African members of the Security Council plus one (A3+), namely Algeria, Guyana, Somalia, and my own country, Sierra Leone.

We welcome the unanimous adoption of the resolution just passed, renewing for twelve months the sanctions regime on Haiti, the targeted arms embargo, and the mandate of the Panel of Experts established pursuant to resolution 2653 (2022). We express our sincere appreciation to the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for their leadership, dedication, and open and constructive approach throughout the negotiation process.

The unanimous support demonstrated today sends an unequivocal, unified message from the Security Council: the international community stands firmly with the people of Haiti in their quest for peace, security, and stability, and will not tolerate those who terrorize Haitian society and undermine its institutions.

The A3+ remains deeply alarmed by the catastrophic security and humanitarian crisis unfolding in Haiti. Armed gangs continue to perpetrate heinous acts of violence against civilians, including targeted assassinations, kidnappings, horrific levels of conflict-related sexual and gender-based violence, and the systematic recruitment and exploitation of children. The displacement of hundreds of thousands of people and severe acute food insecurity compound this tragedy daily.

We reiterate that the illicit flow of firearms, small arms, light weapons, and ammunition into Haiti constitutes the lifeblood of this gang violence. It is unacceptable that heavily armed criminal networks continue to receive advanced weaponry that outguns national security forces. Therefore, the robust enforcement of the territorial arms embargo is paramount. We call on all Member States—particularly countries of origin and transit—to take decisive, concrete measures to intercept illicit shipments, strengthen export and customs controls, and share actionable intelligence with regional and international bodies, including CARICOM IMPACS, UNODC, and INTERPOL.

Equally critical is the targeted sanctions framework. Those who finance, sponsor, arm, and politically protect these criminal gangs must be held accountable. We urge the Sanctions Committee to act decisively and expeditiously to update and expand the sanctions list to target gang leaders and their political and economic backers. 

While targeted sanctions and the arms embargo are indispensable, they must work in concert with wider security, political, and developmental efforts. Following the historic adoption of resolution 2793 (2025) authorizing the transition to the Gang Suppression Force, we emphasize the urgent need for adequate, predictable resources and logistical capabilities to support security operations alongside the Haitian National Police. 

In conclusion, the A3+ reaffirms its unwavering solidarity with the Haitian people. A durable, lasting peace requires not only restoring public safety, but also addressing the structural root causes of poverty, inequality, and institutional fragility, anchored in an inclusive, Haitian-led and Haitian-owned political dialogue aimed at restoring constitutional order.

I thank you.
after.Slovenia:
Slovenia welcomed the unanimous adoption of the resolution renewing the Haiti sanctions regime and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts.

The devastating crisis in Haiti continues to inflict immense suffering on the civilian population. Armed gangs continue to terrorize communities, perpetrating appalling violations of human rights, including widespread sexual and gender-based violence and the systematic recruitment and use of children. 

Targeted sanctions and an effective, fully enforced arms embargo are vital instruments to disrupt the illicit financial networks and arms flows that fuel this horrific violence. Without the steady influx of illicit small arms, light weapons, and ammunition, these criminal gangs would not possess the lethal capacity to hold an entire nation hostage. We therefore strongly call on all Member States, particularly regional states and countries of origin and transit, to effectively implement the arms embargo and step up border, customs, and maritime controls.

We also welcome the explicit focus on accountability for those who violate human rights and exploit vulnerable populations, notably women and children. The work of the Panel of Experts remains essential in providing the Security Council with independent and accurate reporting on sanctions implementation and on the sources and routes of illicit arms and financing.

Finally, Slovenia reaffirms that security measures and sanctions must go hand in hand with a genuine, inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to credible elections and the restoration of democratic institutions, as well as unimpeded humanitarian access to address the acute suffering of the Haitian people.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom welcomes the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution renewing the Haiti sanctions regime and extending the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We thank the co-penholders, Panama and the United States, for their leadership and constructive engagement throughout this process.

Today’s unanimous vote sends a clear and unified message: the international community will not tolerate the actions of those who arm, finance, and fuel the gangs terrorising the Haitian people. 

The proliferation of illicit arms and ammunition into Haiti remains a primary driver of the catastrophic insecurity on the ground. Disrupting these flows and cutting off the financial networks that sustain gang leaders and their political and economic backers is crucial. We urge all Member States, particularly regional partners, to take all necessary measures to implement the arms embargo effectively and to strengthen border and customs controls.

The United Kingdom remains deeply concerned by the staggering levels of violence, and we unequivocally condemn the widespread use of sexual and gender-based violence, as well as the recruitment and exploitation of children by armed gangs. We welcome the explicit focus within this mandate on investigating these egregious violations, and we urge the Sanctions Committee to continue to designate those responsible.

Sanctions are not an end in themselves; they are a critical tool within a broader international effort. Alongside the vital work of the Multinational Security Support mission and its transition to the Gang Suppression Force, we must maintain momentum towards an inclusive, Haitian-led political process leading to free, fair, and credible elections. The United Kingdom remains steadfast in its support for the people of Haiti in their pursuit of peace, security, and justice.
after.United States of America:
The United States thanks our co-penholder, Panama, for its close collaboration and leadership in securing the unanimous adoption of today’s resolution. 

By speaking with one voice today, the Security Council has sent a clear and unequivocal message: the international community will not stand by while violent armed gangs terrorize the Haitian people and threaten the very fabric of the Haitian state. 

Today's renewal of the Haiti sanctions regime, including the targeted arms embargo, travel bans, and asset freezes, along with the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate, is a vital component of our collective strategy to restore security, stability, and rule of law in Haiti. The proliferation of illicit firearms and ammunition into the hands of criminal gangs remains the fuel that drives this crisis, perpetuating horrific acts of murder, kidnapping, widespread sexual and gender-based violence, and the unconscionable recruitment and exploitation of children. 

Stemming the flow of illicit arms into Haiti requires vigilance and decisive action by all Member States. The United States remains firmly committed to holding arms traffickers accountable. We are actively deploying federal law enforcement resources, enhancing border and port inspections, and utilizing legal mechanisms—such as the Bipartisan Safer Communities Act—to investigate, intercept, and prosecute those who smuggle weapons and ammunition from our shores to criminal actors in Haiti. We urge all countries in the region and beyond to implement robust export controls, strengthen customs enforcement, and cooperate fully with international partners, including UNODC, INTERPOL, and CARICOM IMPACS. 

Sanctions are most effective when they adapt to realities on the ground. We call on the 2653 Sanctions Committee to act expeditiously in designating those individuals and entities who support, finance, and arm the gangs, as well as the political and economic elites who exploit chaos for personal gain. There must be accountability for those responsible for atrocities and human rights abuses against civilians. 

Sanctions alone cannot solve the crisis, but together with our recent authorization of the Gang Suppression Force in resolution 2793 (2025), sustained support for the Haitian National Police, the work of BINUH, and urgent humanitarian assistance, we are providing the Haitian people with the tools needed to reclaim their communities. Ultimately, lasting stability requires an inclusive, Haitian-led political process that leads to free, fair, and credible elections. 

The United States stands firmly with the people of Haiti, and we will continue to work closely with the Haitian government, our regional partners, CARICOM, the OAS, and this Council to build a peaceful, secure, and democratic future for Haiti. 

Thank you, Mr. President.
